pageTitle: Classical Guitar: The Art of Finger Mastery
subtitle: Master the art of traditional guitar technique and repertoire

introduction.title: Classical Guitar: The Art of Finger Mastery
introduction.text: Discover the refined world of classical guitar, where centuries of tradition meet sophisticated technique to create some of music's most beautiful sounds.

columns.title: Classical Guitar Hallmarks
columns.text: Nylon strings for warm, mellow tone. Fingerstyle technique without picks. Wide neck for complex fingerings. Rich classical and flamenco repertoire. Emphasis on proper posture and technique.

cards.title: Classical Guitar
items: Strings: Nylon (trebles) and wound nylon/silver (basses)
Neck: Wide (2" at nut), flat fretboard
Sound: Warm, mellow, intimate
Technique: Fingerstyle only, classical position
Repertoire: Classical, flamenco, bossa nova
Volume: Quieter, perfect for solo performance

cards.title: Steel-String Acoustic
items: Strings: Steel core with bronze/phosphor bronze wrap
Neck: Narrower (1.75" typical), radiused fretboard
Sound: Bright, projective, cutting
Technique: Picks, strumming, various positions
Repertoire: Folk, country, rock, pop
Volume: Louder, cuts through band mix

cards.title: Construction Details
items: Nylon Strings: Gentle on fingers, warm tone, traditional sound
Wide Neck: Usually 2" at nut, accommodates fingerstyle technique
Flat Fretboard: No radius for classical playing position
Traditional Bridge: Tie-block system for string attachment

cards.title: Wood Selection
items: Spruce Top: Most common, bright and responsive
Cedar Top: Warmer, immediate response, popular choice
Rosewood Back/Sides: Rich overtones, traditional choice
Cypress Back/Sides: Flamenco favorite, bright and percussive

fields.label: Body Position
fields.value: Sit on front edge of chair; back straight, relaxed shoulders; left foot elevated on footstool; guitar rests on left thigh; guitar at 45-degree angle

fields.label: Hand Position
fields.value: Left thumb behind neck, not wrapped; right hand curved, fingers approach strings at angle; wrist straight, not bent; fingertips perpendicular to strings; relaxed, natural movement

cards.title: Modern Alternatives
cards.description: Many players now use guitar supports, cushions, or straps to achieve the proper playing angle without a footstool, reducing strain.
items: Ergoplay or A-Frame supports
Cushions and pillows
Classical guitar straps
Adjustable height chairs

cards.title: Rest Stroke (Apoyando)
cards.description: Finger plucks through string and rests on next string

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Powerful, focused tone; good for melodies; traditional technique

fields.label: Best Used For
fields.value: Scales, single-note passages, emphasized notes

cards.title: Free Stroke (Tirando)
cards.description: Finger plucks string without touching adjacent strings

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Allows chord playing; lighter touch; more versatile

fields.label: Best Used For
fields.value: Arpeggios, chords, rapid passages

cards.title: Tremolo
cards.description: Rapid repetition of single note with a-m-i fingers

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Creates sustained melody effect; beautiful classical sound; advanced expression

fields.label: Best Used For
fields.value: Romantic pieces, Spanish repertoire

cards.title: Rasgueado
cards.description: Flamenco strumming technique with multiple fingers

fields.label: Benefits
fields.value: Percussive rhythm; flamenco authenticity; dynamic expression

fields.label: Best Used For
fields.value: Flamenco music, rhythmic accompaniment

fields.label: Key Composers
fields.value: John Dowland, Gaspar Sanz, Robert de Visee, Sylvius Leopold Weiss

fields.label: Essential Works
fields.value: Dowland Lute Songs; Bach BWV 996-1000; Weiss Sonatas

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Lute transcriptions, contrapuntal textures, dance forms

fields.label: Key Composers

fields.label: Essential Works
fields.value: Sor Studies; Giuliani Concertos; Tarrega Recuerdos de la Alhambra

fields.label: Characteristics

fields.label: Key Composers
fields.value: Heitor Villa-Lobos, Leo Brouwer, Joaquin Rodrigo, Roland Dyens

fields.label: Essential Works
fields.value: Villa-Lobos Preludes; Rodrigo Concierto de Aranjuez; Brouwer Etudes

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Extended techniques, world music influences, avant-garde approaches

cards.title: The Spanish Tradition
cards.description: Flamenco guitar shares the nylon-string construction of classical guitar but emphasizes rhythm, percussion, and passionate expression.

fields.label: Flamenco Differences
fields.value: Lower string action for percussive effects; cypress back/sides for brighter tone; tap plates (golpeadores) to protect top; more aggressive playing style; emphasis on rhythm and passion

fields.label: Key Techniques
fields.value: Rasgueado (flamenco strumming); golpe (percussive tapping); alzapua (thumb technique); picado (fast scale passages); tremolo (rapid note repetition)

cards.title: Student ($200-800)
tableRows: Solid spruce top, perfect starter guitar

cards.title: Intermediate ($800-2500)
tableRows: Cedar top, Indian rosewood, excellent value

fields.label: Technique
fields.value: Proper posture and hand position; rest stroke and free stroke; basic scales and arpeggios; simple chord progressions

fields.label: Repertoire
fields.value: Beginner method books (Carcassi, etc.); simple classical pieces; folk song arrangements; basic sight-reading

fields.label: Advanced Technique
fields.value: Barre chords and advanced fingerings; tremolo technique; advanced arpeggios and scales; dynamic control and expression

fields.label: Intermediate Repertoire
fields.value: Sor studies and sonatinas; Bach lute suites (easier movements); Villa-Lobos Preludes; Spanish pieces (Tarrega)

fields.label: Advanced Skills
fields.value: Concert-level technique; extended techniques; interpretation and style; performance preparation

fields.label: Advanced Repertoire
fields.value: Major concertos (Rodrigo, etc.); complete Bach lute suites; modern masterworks; personal interpretation development

cards.title: Effective Practice
items: Slow practice: Build muscle memory correctly
Metronome use: Develop steady rhythm
Repetition: Perfect small sections before combining
Mental practice: Study scores away from guitar
Recording: Listen to your playing objectively

cards.title: Physical Wellness
items: Posture breaks: Avoid strain and injury
Hand exercises: Maintain flexibility
Gradual increase: Build endurance slowly
Proper warm-up: Scales and technical exercises
Relaxation: Stay loose and natural
